themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. So the models try to make honesty pay: a faster lane, a better price, a perk for whoever declares themselves.
themes.evidence: On governing agentic traffic all three models said agents gain by passing as human and offered incentives instead of rules (a discount for proving delegation, a fast checkout lane, a signed pilot), and the same money-and-politics blocker runs through journey orchestration, the semantic context layer, and ad supply integrity.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own from cases they already know for certain.
themes.evidence: On governing agentic traffic, Claude would tag orders known to come through an agent and label the sessions behind them, and ChatGPT would build clearly labeled sessions through a pilot; the same move appears in identity resolution panels, answer engine prompt panels, and incrementality holdouts.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution draws proxies, gateways and spend caps from all three models, governing agentic traffic draws signed permission tokens and a dedicated agent endpoint, and downstream consent draws a single checkpoint on every path data leaves the building.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and guess whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models call black-box platforms and already-trained models unprovable, and the same wall shows up in incrementality (platforms control both the treatment and the evidence) and in ad supply integrity.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers all converge on an approved-claims registry while admitting implied claims need a human, and the semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions of customer a political settlement rather than a modeling gap.
